findings.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full Zod SafeParseResult ({ success, data }) which is assigned directly to key and persisted via prisma.credential.update, corrupting the stored credential by saving { success: true, data: {...} } instead of the parsed Google credentials object

refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response object when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, but callers expect the parsed token data structure and access properties like .access_token or .data.error that don't exist on a Response, causing runtime errors or undefined behavior
Zoho Bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, sending the wrong identifier to the credential sync endpoint

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] which both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]', causing a key collision where the second overwrites the first and the schema does not match its intended design

After safeParse, the code accesses refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token but neither minimumTokenResponseSchema nor caller schemas like salesforceTokenSchema declare a refresh_token field, resulting in a TypeScript error and a no-op mutation for the minimum-schema path

Salesforce CalendarService fetches a fresh access token and updates prisma.credential but returns new jsforce.Connection without passing the newly fetched accessToken or instanceUrl, so the connection is not constructed with the refreshed tokens and the refresh call serves no purpose in the local path

Webhook endpoint has no HTTP method restriction - handler does not check req.method, allowing any HTTP method (GET, PUT, DELETE, etc.) which could enable CSRF attacks via GET requests or unintended processing of non-POST methods

minimumTokenResponseSchema computed property keys are broken - z.string().toString() evaluates to '[object Object]' for both computed keys, causing the second to overwrite the first, making the 'minimum token response' fallback path non-functional

Google Calendar stores SafeParseResult instead of parsed data as credential key - parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParseResult object but the code stores it directly as key in prisma.credential.update, corrupting the stored credential

refreshOAuthTokens returns fundamentally incompatible types across code paths - returns a Response from fetch() when credential sharing is enabled but returns varying types when disabled, breaking callers like Hubspot and Zoho at runtime

Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens - the variable credentialId is passed where userId: number | null is expected, unlike all other adapters which pass credential.userId

No error handling for decryption or JSON parsing in webhook handler - symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse are not wrapped in try-catch, causing unhandled 500 errors with stack traces instead of clean error responses
Zod validation failure in webhook handler produces 500 instead of 400 - appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError on invalid input with no surrounding try-catch

refreshOAuthTokens does not check response.ok for credential sync endpoint - the fetch response is returned directly without checking response.ok, causing callers to try parsing error bodies as valid token responses
No authentication sent to credential sync endpoint - the POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT includes no authentication headers, a security gap given the endpoint receives user IDs and app slugs

parseRefreshTokenResponse injects placeholder 'refresh_token' string when refresh_token is missing from parsed data, which would be persisted and used on subsequent refresh attempts, silently breaking token refresh

Salesforce token refresh runs unconditionally on every service instantiation - the refresh token fetch executes in the constructor regardless of token validity, causing unnecessary API calls unlike other adapters
Salesforce uses fragile response.statusText !== 'OK' for error detection - statusText varies across HTTP implementations and locales, should use response.ok or response.status

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is not a boolean - the expression evaluates to the string value of CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY or undefined, not true/false, which could cause subtle bugs if compared with === true or serialized
No tests for new webhook endpoint or utility functions - the PR adds a webhook endpoint, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and refreshOAuthTokens but includes no unit or integration tests
Salesforce refresh path in CalendarService.ts (~line 75-100) bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, calling the refresh endpoint directly, so credential sync silently never applies to Salesforce

minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-12 is broken — z.string().toString() yields '[object Object]' so the dynamic keys collapse and the schema only validates access_token, dropping all other fields like expiry and refresh_token

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 defaults refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token', which combined with the schema bug will persist 'refresh_token: "refresh_token"' into user credentials on every sync-enabled refresh, corrupting stored credentials and breaking subsequent refreshes

Google, Hubspot, Zoho-Bigin, and Zoho-CRM refresh paths have a contract mismatch on the sync branch — refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response but callers expect already-parsed data and never call .json() on it, making the sync path non-functional
zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:91 passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, sending the wrong identifier to the sync endpoint
zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 replaces ${appConfig.slug} with a hardcoded literal 'zoho-bigin' string in the redirect URI, which is unrelated to OAuth credential sync and constitutes scope drift

parseRefreshTokenResponse is only adopted in Google, Office365 Calendar, Zoom, and Salesforce — Hubspot, Lark, Office365 Video, Webex, Zoho-Bigin, and Zoho-CRM call refreshOAuthTokens but never parse the response, leaving the sync-validation contract half-wired
.env.example:244 recommends 'openssl rand -base64 24' for CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY which produces 24 bytes, not the required 32 bytes; it should be 'openssl rand -base64 32'
turbo.json:202-205 places CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, breaking the consistent alphabetical grouping of CALCOM_* env vars before CALENDSO_* vars

File-move refactor (renaming createOAuthAppCredential, decodeOAuthState, encodeOAuthState into a new oauth/ subfolder and updating ~20 import paths) is bundled into a feature PR, inflating the diff and increasing merge conflict risk

Credential key shape changed from parsed data to `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: {...} }` which is stored directly as `key`, so `credential.key.access_token` is `undefined` on next load, breaking Google Calendar integration even when credential sharing is disabled

Authentication bypass when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset — `undefined !== undefined` evaluates to `false`, so if both env var and header are absent the auth check passes, allowing unauthenticated credential writes

Zod computed property keys in `parseRefreshTokenResponse` evaluate to the same string `"[object Object]"` because `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` produce identical keys, making the second property overwrite the first and resulting in a no-op schema that only validates `access_token`

`refresh_token` silently overwritten with the literal string `"refresh_token"` when the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, which is then persisted to the credential `key` in the database and sent to the OAuth provider on the next refresh, permanently losing the original refresh token

Type/shape mismatch in Google Calendar: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch.Response` when sharing is enabled but the caller expects a Google auth response with `.data`, causing `token` to be `undefined` and a `TypeError` on next line

Type/shape mismatch in HubSpot: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch.Response` when sharing is enabled but the caller expects a `HubspotToken`, so accesses to `.access_token`, `.refresh_token`, and `.expiry_date` all return `undefined`

Type/shape mismatch in Zoho Bigin: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch.Response` when sharing is enabled but the caller expects an AxiosResponse with `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `tokenInfo.data.error` throws a `TypeError`
Type/shape mismatch in Zoho CRM: same AxiosResponse vs `fetch.Response` mismatch as Zoho Bigin, causing `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` and `.access_token` to throw a `TypeError`

TOCTOU race condition in webhook: `findFirst` + `create` with no unique constraint or transaction allows two concurrent webhook calls for the same `(userId, appId)` to both return null and both create duplicate credentials
No HTTP method check in webhook handler — it does not verify `req.method === "POST"`, allowing credential writes via GET, DELETE, or any other HTTP method

Unhandled exceptions from `Zod.parse()` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` with no try/catch result in unstructured 500 errors instead of clean 400/403; additionally `symmetricDecrypt` silently falls back to an empty-string key if the env var is unset

Salesforce error check uses `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of `response.ok` or `response.status` — `statusText` is locale-dependent and can vary across proxy/CDN layers, causing false failures on valid 200 responses
No timeout on `fetch` to credential sync endpoint in `refreshOAuthTokens` — if the external endpoint hangs, the entire OAuth refresh path blocks indefinitely with no fallback
No `response.ok` check on credential sync endpoint response — a 500/404/HTML error page is returned as-is and downstream callers attempt to parse it as valid token JSON, producing confusing failures

No authentication sent on outgoing `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` — the incoming webhook requires a secret header, but the outgoing request sends no auth headers, API key, or signature, allowing impersonation of any user's token refresh

`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is `string | undefined`, not a boolean — `process.env.X && process.env.Y` returns the second string or `undefined`, which fails strict equality checks and type narrowing

Feature flag checks are inconsistent — `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` checks two env vars but `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally checks `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, so the flag can be "enabled" while the sync endpoint is unset, creating a semantically incoherent state

Token refresh runs unconditionally on every Salesforce connection instantiation in the constructor path, not just when expired like other adapters, risking rate-limiting and unnecessary latency on every booking page load or event operation

Salesforce refresh does not use `refreshOAuthTokens` and instead does a raw `fetch`, bypassing credential sync entirely and making it inconsistent with the PR's stated purpose of wrapping all adapters in `refreshOAuthTokens`

Return type of `refreshOAuthTokens` is `any`, defeating compile-time detection of the shape mismatches where callers in Google, HubSpot, Zoho Bigin, and Zoho CRM access properties that don't exist on a `fetch.Response`
Encryption key generation command in `.env.example` produces 24 bytes (`openssl rand -base64 24`) instead of the 32 bytes required for AES-256, resulting in AES-192 entropy
refreshOAuthTokens.ts return type inconsistency causes runtime errors when sharing is enabled, as it returns a raw fetch Response instead of provider-specific responses expected by callers

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:93 saves the Zod safeParse wrapper object instead of .data when persisting credentials
zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:88 passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, sending the wrong identifier to the sync endpoint

IDOR / Broken Access Control: Webhook endpoint takes userId directly from request body with no per-user authorization or tenant scoping, allowing anyone with the shared webhook secret to create or overwrite OAuth credentials for any user

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint has no HTTP method restriction - handler does not check req.method, allowing any HTTP method (GET, PUT, DELETE, etc.) which could enable CSRF attacks via GET requests or unintended processing of non-POST methods

adjudication.rationale: In the new Next.js API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the `handler` never checks `req.method` (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). As written, Next.js will route any HTTP method (GET/PUT/DELETE/etc.) into the same logic path, and the code will attempt to authenticate and then `parse(req.body)` regardless of method. This is a verifiable absence in the diff and can lead to unintended invocation/behavior for non-POST methods (even if the header secret check mitigates casual CSRF).

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns fundamentally incompatible types across code paths - returns a Response from fetch() when credential sharing is enabled but returns varying types when disabled, breaking callers like Hubspot and Zoho at runtime

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the function returns a `fetch()` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, but returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns otherwise. Callers rely on specific shapes: e.g. Google Calendar now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` which works for the disabled path (it returns `fetchTokens.res` from `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken`, which has `.data`), but will fail in the enabled path because a `Response` has no `.data`. Hubspot assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and later uses it as a token object; in the enabled path it will instead be a `Response`, breaking at runtime. This incompatibility is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling for decryption or JSON parsing in webhook handler - symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse are not wrapped in try-catch, causing unhandled 500 errors with stack traces instead of clean error responses

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no `try/catch`. Both `symmetricDecrypt(...)` (e.g., wrong/empty key, malformed ciphertext) and `JSON.parse(...)` (non-JSON plaintext) can throw, which will bubble out of the handler and result in an unhandled 500 response rather than a controlled error JSON. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` and does not include any authentication material (no headers, no token/secret in the body, no signature). This is directly verifiable in the diff. Given the endpoint is intended to return refreshed OAuth access tokens for a given `calcomUserId`/`appSlug`, the lack of an authentication mechanism from Cal.com to that endpoint is a legitimate security/design gap: the receiving service has no built-in way to verify the caller is Cal.com beyond external measures (e.g., network ACLs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-12 is broken — z.string().toString() yields '[object Object]' so the dynamic keys collapse and the schema only validates access_token, dropping all other fields like expiry and refresh_token

Either way, the intended validation behavior is broken in the diff.

Call sites then proceed as if the refresh succeeded and attempt to consume token-shaped data (e.g., Office365/Teams call `handleErrorsJson(response)` and then `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`; if the endpoint returns a 404/500 or non-JSON body, the downstream parsing will fail in a confusing way rather than raising a clear "sync endpoint failed" error at the boundary).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:39 throws an unhandled ZodError on malformed request body, resulting in an unstructured 500 response instead of a clean 400
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and candidate issue describe the same problem: using `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` without handling `ZodError` causes invalid/malformed request bodies to throw, leading to a 500 Internal Server Error (unstructured) instead of returning an expected 400 Bad Request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lacks an HTTP method restriction, allowing GET, PUT, DELETE, etc. to create or update credentials

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` exports a single `handler(req, res)` that performs auth checks and then immediately parses `req.body` and writes to Prisma, but it never checks `req.method` (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). In Next.js API routes, the handler is invoked for any HTTP method, so requests using GET/PUT/DELETE/etc. that include the expected header + body could reach the same create/update logic. Therefore the diff does introduce the lack of an HTTP method restriction as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-27 compares the webhook secret with non-constant-time !==, making it vulnerable to timing attacks

adjudication.rationale:
In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler checks the webhook secret via a direct inequality comparison:

req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET

This uses normal JS string comparison rather than a constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on Buffers). That is a verifiable property of the diff and is a recognized security weakness for secret validation because it can leak information via timing differences.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not include `packages/lib/constants.ts` (or any lines 102-103), so the claimed typing of `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` as `string | undefined` cannot be verified from the provided changes. adjudication_records.issue_text: IDOR / Broken Access Control: Webhook endpoint takes userId directly from request body with no per-user authorization or tenant scoping, allowing anyone with the shared webhook secret to create or overwrite OAuth credentials for any user

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` accepts `userId` and `appSlug` from the request body and then updates/creates a `credential` row for that `userId` (`prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` followed by `update`/`create`). The only authorization check is a single instance-wide shared secret comparison against a header (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] !== CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). There is no per-user authorization, no tenant/team scoping, and no check that the caller is entitled to modify credentials for the specified `userId`. Therefore, any party that knows the shared webhook secret can overwrite/create OAuth credentials for arbitrary users by supplying a different `userId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse: z.string().toString() returns '[object Object]' causing both computed keys to collapse to the same string, resulting in token-refresh responses being validated against an incorrect schema that silently drops refresh_token, expiry_date, scope, and other fields

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed keys are evaluated immediately to a single literal string (very likely the same for both, e.g. "[object Object]" or a Zod string name), so this does not create an index signature for arbitrary expiry fields. It instead defines one (or effectively one) specific property name, making the schema incorrect for real token responses. Additionally, because the schema is not `.passthrough()`/`.catchall(...)`, Zod will strip unknown fields by default, so fields like `expiry_date`, `scope`, etc. will be dropped from `refreshTokenResponse.data`, matching the finding’s impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-constant-time webhook secret comparison: shared secret compared with JavaScript's !== operator which short-circuits on first character mismatch, creating a timing side-channel that allows progressive secret recovery

adjudication.rationale:
The new webhook handler compares the provided secret directly with `!==`:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

In JavaScript/Node, normal string equality/inequality is not guaranteed to be constant-time and typically exits as soon as a mismatch is found (after length checks), which can create a timing side-channel for shared-secret verification. A constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over same-length buffers) is the standard mitigation for this class of issue when comparing secrets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated outgoing requests to credential sync endpoint: Cal.com sends userId and appSlug to the sync endpoint with no authentication header, signature, or shared secret, allowing anyone who knows the endpoint URL to trigger credential-refresh logic for arbitrary users

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) sends a POST to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only a `URLSearchParams` body containing `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, and no authentication mechanism (no header, signature, shared secret, etc.). This is verifiable in the diff. While the impact depends on how the external endpoint is implemented, Cal.com provides no way for that endpoint to verify the caller, so the finding about unauthenticated outgoing requests is grounded in the code change (even though the "anyone who knows the endpoint URL" part describes the receiver-side exposure).
